title: Bilateral Reference for High-Resolution Dichotomous Image Segmentation (BiRefNet)
mechanism: Reconstruction module re-injects hierarchical raw image patches at each decoder stage (source reference) and uses gradient maps as target reference with auxiliary gradient supervision, for very thin high-res structures.
adaptation: Cheap: pixel-unshuffle the raw 512 px EL cell into each decoder scale of U-Net++ and add a gradient-map auxiliary loss restricted to a 3 px band around crack and gridline labels. Bench: BiRefNet as a binary crack segmenter at 512 px.
min_experiment: Arm: house PF + image re-injection + band gradient loss; baseline: house PF; CV gridline IoU and crack IoU. Kill if gridline IoU < +0.03 and crack IoU n.d.
evidence: R: abstract claims best results on four tasks (DIS, HRSOD, COD, etc.); numbers not retrieved.
prior_overlap: R5 (2x input) n.d. covers more pixels per crack, not raw-image re-injection or gradient supervision. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Pixel-unshuffle the raw 512 px EL cell into each decoder scale of U-Net++; gradient-map auxiliary loss only in a 3 px band around crack and gridline labels so it does not learn grain texture. Also run full BiRefNet as a binary crack bench entry.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm house PF + image re-injection + banded gradient loss vs house PF; 5-fold CV crack relF1@2, gridline IoU; kill: gridline < +0.03 and crack n.d. About 12 GPU-h.
